title: Privacy Pipeline: Scan Progress & Stall Detection
description: PII scan throughput and the sent-minus-received stall detector. Built to catch the silent wedge described in NXE-2480.

panels.title: ⭐ PIT LEASE MARGIN — the actual failure predictor
Estimated max search gap
panels.description:
consumers x page_size / throughput, in seconds.

Compare against $lease (ES_PIT_KEEP_ALIVE, default 1800s). Above the lease, the next search returns 404 search_context_missing_exception and the scan dies silently — privacy discards the reader error, so the job still reports SUCCESS.

Green below 900s (half the lease). Red at 1800s.

panels.title: Search gap vs PIT lease
panels.description: The flat reference line is the lease. Any time the gap crosses it, the PIT is already dead — the scan just has not found out yet, because it only discovers this on its NEXT search.

panels.title: Critical throughput
panels.description:
The document rate below which the PIT cannot survive:

    consumers x page_size / lease

At 32 consumers, 1000-doc pages and a 30m lease this is 17.8 docs/s. Anything slower is living on borrowed time.

Note this is 32x higher than the naive 'one search per page' figure of 0.556 docs/s — that number is the AVERAGE search rate and it does not predict failure.

panels.title: Document throughput vs critical rate
panels.description: Blue is what the pipeline is actually draining. Red is the critical rate from the panel to the left. Blue below red means the lease will expire.

panels.title: THE STALL DETECTOR — read this first
Fetches in flight (sent - received)
panels.description:
THE single most important number on this dashboard, and it needs no code change.

oscillating near 0     -> healthy
FLAT at worker count   -> every fetch worker is blocked. THE SCAN IS WEDGED.
climbing steadily      -> content-service falling behind

A flat plateau lasting longer than the PIT keep-alive (30m) means the scan is already dead and does not know it yet.

panels.title: In-flight fetches over time — FLAT LINE = WEDGED
panels.description:
Watch the SHAPE, not the value. A healthy scan is sawtoothed. A horizontal line at the fetch-worker count is the failure: workers blocked forever on replies that will never arrive.

NOTE: the worker count is currently ambiguous — values.yaml sets PIPELINE_CONSUMERS=16 in the env block while the configmap renders pipelineConsumers=4. Resolve this before interpreting the plateau height.

targets.expr: sum by (job_id) (pii_docs_sent_total{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", job_id=~"$job_id"}) - sum by (job_id) (pii_docs_received_total{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", job_id=~"$job_id"})

panels.title: Documents still unaccounted
panels.description: Dispatched but neither analysed nor failed. Should trend to 0 at scan end. A persistent non-zero residue is silently lost work.

targets.expr: sum(pii_docs_sent_total{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", job_id=~"$job_id"}) - sum(pii_docs_processed_total{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", job_id=~"$job_id"}) - sum(pii_errors_total{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", job_id=~"$job_id", kind="get_content"})

panels.title: Funnel rates — these four lines should track each other
panels.description:
Divergence localises the bottleneck:
sent >> received    -> content-service (the hypothesis)
received >> analysed-> PII analysis CPU-bound
analysed >> persisted-> OpenSearch bulk writer is the constraint

That last case is the main ALTERNATIVE explanation for a stalled scan and is cheap to rule out here.

panels.title: Drop-off between stages (cumulative gaps)
panels.description: Each series is a queue depth. Whichever grows without bound is the constraint.

panels.title: Error rate by kind
panels.description:
kind='get_content' is privacy's own view of content-service failing it.

IMPORTANT: with CONTENT_GET_TIMEOUT unset this counter UNDERSTATES reality. A lost reply produces no error at all — the worker just waits forever. Setting CONTENT_GET_TIMEOUT=300s is what makes this metric start telling the truth.

panels.title: Per-document processing time (SEE DESCRIPTION — buckets are wrong)
panels.description:
CURRENTLY NEARLY USELESS. This histogram uses prometheus.DefBuckets, whose top bucket is 10 SECONDS, on a path where a 120s extraction is normal. Essentially everything interesting lands in +Inf and these quantiles are extrapolated fiction.

FIX: explicit buckets {0.5,1,2.5,5,10,30,60,120,240,300} in internal/metrics/metrics.go. Until then use the >10s counter beside this.

panels.title: Documents slower than 10s (top bucket overflow)
panels.description: The honest version of the panel beside this one: a straight count of documents exceeding the largest usable bucket.

targets.expr: sum(rate(pii_doc_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", job_id=~"$job_id", le="+Inf"}[5m])) - sum(rate(pii_doc_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", job_id=~"$job_id", le="10"}[5m]))

panels.title: Scrape & pod health — privacy scales to zero, so read this before trusting anything above
Scrape up/down — GAPS ARE EXPECTED
panels.description:
privacyBeGo autoscaling.minReplicas defaults to 0 and the PodMonitor scrapes every 30s. Short scans may be scraped once or not at all, and every counter RESETS on a new pod.

Practical consequences:
- rate() over a resetting counter is unreliable
- an empty panel means 'no pod', NOT 'no problem'
- prefer the equivalent content-service panel where one exists (minReplicas:1, continuous series)
- pin replicas during any investigation

panels.title: CPU vs limit
panels.description: Privacy pods are Guaranteed QoS (requests == limits). PIPELINE_GOMAXPROCS is set to 2 because there is no automaxprocs and NumCPU() reports NODE cores.

panels.title: Replica count (KEDA)
panels.description: Scale-from-zero latency is bounded by KEDA pollingInterval (30s). Metrics before the pod exists are simply absent.

panels.title: ⭐ EXTRACTOR — PIT expiry, the OBSERVED failure signal
PIT expiries ($__range)
panels.description:
extractor_pit_renewals_total is incremented ONLY when a search fails with search_context_missing_exception and the reader rebuilds the PIT to resume. ANY non-zero value means a slice stalled long enough to lose its lease — the NXE-2480 condition, observed rather than modelled.

Compare with 'Estimated max search gap' at the top: that panel PREDICTS this one. If the estimate is under the lease and this is non-zero, the model's inputs (consumers/batch/lease) are wrong.

Note maxPitRenewals = 3: after three consecutive renewals a slice gives up and the remaining documents are dropped. There is no metric for that yet.

panels.title: PIT expiries over time, by scan job
panels.description: When the lease was lost, and for which job. Correlate the timestamps against 'Search gap vs PIT lease' above — an expiry should land shortly after the modelled gap crosses the lease line. If it lands earlier, the consumer/batch assumptions need revisiting.

panels.title: Publish failures ($__range)
panels.description: extractor_publish_failures_total counts ItemBatches that could not be handed to the next pipeline stage. Its own source comment notes these 'were previously discarded silently' — the same class of bug as the NXE-2480 truncation. Non-zero means documents were read from OpenSearch and then lost before privacy ever saw them.

panels.title: Item conversion errors by connector type
panels.description: extractor_item_conversion_errors_total fires when a document in the index cannot be turned into a pipeline Item. Directly relevant to the V1.5 -> V2 reindex work: the CIFS and Box converters hard-fail an item with no source_url, so a migration that omitted it shows up here as a steady error rate for that connector_type.
